successors.note: The state was a federal state of the German Empire from 1871 and ended in November 1918 (see the dissolve event); the Weimar Republic took over its land (Free State of Oldenburg). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-53 D01, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire; same change as fx-46 R122 for Bavaria); the hierarchy.csv row duchy-of-oldenburg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator.

The infobox has 'Raised to duchy: 1774' and the text 'in 1777 the county was raised to the rank of a duchy'; the duchy existed before the dossier's 1806 start, so the found event stays at Cliopatria's first year, confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1810: France annexes Oldenburg on 13 December 1810. The Confederation page's table: Oldenburg, joined 14 October 1808, 'Annexed by France on 13 December 1810'; the Duchy page: 'Between 1810 and 1814, Oldenburg was occupied by Napoleonic France' and the Bouches-du-Weser page lists an arrondissement of Oldenburg in the department formed in 1811. Eutin, annexed separately into the Bouches de l'Elbe, has its own event.

ledger.note: 1813: William I is restored and the duchy returns. Infobox: 'William I: 1785-1810, restored 1813-23'; the page also has the occupation lasting 'between 1810 and 1814' and Cliopatria's shape resumes in 1814; the Bouches-du-Weser page: 'After Napoleon was defeated in 1814, the department was divided' among Hanover, Oldenburg and Bremen. The month is on no page. Eutin is not in this region: the Prince-Bishopric of Lübeck page has it annexed to France until 1814.

ledger.note: 1814: Eutin returns to the Duchy of Oldenburg. The principality was annexed to France 'between 1810 and 1814' and 'then returned to the Duchy of Oldenburg' (Prince-Bishopric of Lübeck page); the German Grand Duchy page has Peter Friedrich Ludwig return from exile in 1814. No month.

1815: the duchy becomes the Grand Duchy of Oldenburg. 'Oldenburg was elevated to a grand duchy at the Congress of Vienna'; the first two grand dukes still styled themselves dukes and Peter I took the grand-ducal title in 1823.

region.text: the Principality of Birkenfeld, 'on 16 April 1817, Oldenburg took possession of the region'

ledger.note: 1817: Oldenburg takes possession of the Principality of Birkenfeld on 16 April 1817. Prussia 'agreed [at the Congress of Vienna, 1815] that, in view of its territorial gains in the Saar region' it would hand over the area as compensation; the final allocation was made by the Territorial Commission of the Great Powers in Frankfurt (Birkenfeld page). The Duchy page dates the acquisition to 1815 ('In 1815, the Duchy acquired the Principality of Birkenfeld and became a grand duchy'); the drawn gain follows the possession. The gazetteer lacks Birkenfeld; the 13 km circle is a placement. The page names Prussia as the ceding party.

region.text: the Lordship of Jever (a 12 km circle round Jever; the place is not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1818: Oldenburg annexes the Lordship of Jever. 'The Lordship of Jever ceased to exist as a separate entity when it was fully annexed by Oldenburg in 1818.' The page records Jever's holders: the Anhalt-Zerbst line to 1793, then Catherine the Great of Russia, the Kingdom of Holland in 1807, the French department Ems-Oriental in 1810; it does not say who ceded it in 1818.

Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

notes: REPAIR (batch eu-20-e, 2026-11-01). Cliopatria's Oldenburg outline stops at 8.47 E and lacks Delmenhorst, Vechta and the Weser bank at Brake (reviewer's polygon test; at cell level Wildeshausen and Elsfleth are inside, Delmenhorst, Vechta and Brake are not). From 1820 Cliopatria's Birkenfeld cell (7.46 E 49.69 N) lies one cell east of Birkenfeld town (7.24/49.66), so it is replaced by the 13 km Birkenfeld circle of 1817-1819. Every keyframe is adjust: Cliopatria's shape of the year plus Eutin (13 km circle), Delmenhorst (10 km), Vechta (8 km), Wildeshausen (8 km, no new cell) and Brake (10 km); 24-30 grid cells (6,100-7,600 km2 on a 253 km2 cell) against the 6,420 km2 of the German Confederation page, which includes Birkenfeld and Eutin (ratio of the Cliopatria polygons alone 0.68-0.76). Delmenhorst: Cliopatria files its two cells under the Free City of Bremen; free-city-of-bremen is redrawn on the city itself and leaves Delmenhorst to this dossier (agreed in the repair of both). Re-dated from pages: Birkenfeld possession 16 April 1817 (Birkenfeld page; Prussia ceded it, agreed at the Congress of Vienna 1815), so the 1815 keyframe ends in 1816 and a new 1817 keyframe carries Birkenfeld; Eutin annexed to France 1810-1814 (Prince-Bishopric of Lübeck page), so it is left out of the 1813 keyframe and returns in 1814. 1811-1812 are deliberately empty (annexed). DISAGREEMENTS: duchy raised in 1774 (infobox) or 1777 (text); restoration 1813 (rulers, 'restored 1813-23') or 1814 (occupation 'between 1810 and 1814'; German Grand Duchy page: Peter Friedrich Ludwig back in 1814; Bouches-du-Weser: 'After Napoleon was defeated in 1814'). SILENCES: the Jade Treaty of 1853 (the German Grand Duchy page has the Jade area to Prussia in 1853 without a treaty name) and Kniphausen; who ceded Jever (the German page: the Tsar, in 1818); Cliopatria's 1834-1864 area steps. Eutin, Birkenfeld, Jever, Delmenhorst, Vechta and Brake are drawn as lon/lat circles (Eutin 10.62 E 54.14 N; Birkenfeld 7.16 E 49.65 N; Jever 7.90 E 53.57 N); the gazetteer agent may add the places. 'principality-of-birkenfeld' (optional: an Oldenburg exclave, ceded by Prussia) and 'lordship-of-jever' need dossiers. Pages budget: 5 original plus 4 in the repair (German Grand Duchy of Oldenburg, Prince-Bishopric of Lübeck, Principality of Birkenfeld, German Confederation). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (duchy-of-oldenburg_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row duchy-of-oldenburg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. The Grand Duchy page gives 9 November 1918 only as the infobox revolution date and no abdication day.
